card.name: Words just before cause-and-effect terms
card.fires_on: Words in warning sections that come right before a causal phrase, such as 'drug' in 'antipsychotic drug products differ in their potential to cause'. Also fires partway through section headings like 'Potential Impacts' and 'Acute Gout'.

modes.label: Noun before 'potential to cause'
modes.description: The word 'drug' after 'antipsychotic' or 'history of', ahead of a phrase about causing or inducing an effect.
modes.example: Whether antipsychotic<< drug>> products differ in their potential to cause tard

modes.label: Inside warning headings
modes.description: A word or word start within a section heading, such as Potential Impacts or Acute Gout.
modes.example: 2.5 Acute<< G>>out The recommended starting dose

modes.label: Possessive or adjective before a mechanism
modes.description: A word like 'their' or 'potential' that introduces an action or trigger.
modes.example: Through<< their>> primary action, cholinesterase inhibitors

card.writes: It favors words like 'contains' and 'includes' and suppresses causal verbs like causes, promotes and triggers.
card.plain: It fires on words in warning text that come just before a statement of what a drug might cause.
